lee: Heads up — after yesterday's allocator hotswap on staging I'm seeing a weird interaction between KV prefill + slab fragmentation that spikes OOMs for long-chat requests. attaching quick profiler snippet below and a short timeline

ana: can you paste the pprof flame or a short heap summary? wondering if the new slab sizes are leaving many small unusable fragments

lee: paste of `pprof --text` (trimmed):
```
TotalAlloc = 1320MB
in-use-bytes = 912MB
free-fragments = 78 (avg 8.3KB)
largest-free-block = 48MB
workspace_reserve = 64MB
kv_cache_allocated = 420MB
kv_prefill_reserved = 256MB
OOMs(last 1h)=7
```

lee: baseline before hotswap: free-fragments 24, largest-free-block 112MB, OOMs=1

tj: rough take: hotswap moved to smaller slab buckets to reduce average waste, but that can blow up fragmentation when KV prefill reserves contiguous ranges for long requests. prefill >=256MB + per-request decode allocations eats continuous blocks -> OOMs

ana: trying to repro with microbench — running this harness now: `tools/bench/run_kv_synth.sh --seq-len 2048 --prefill 256 --concurrency 50`

infra-bot: deploy/staging 1758894240 started by lee — rolling allocator patch v2 (no downtime expected) :rocket:

lee: experiment idea: two short flips
1) lower per-request kv cap from 1Gi -> 512Mi and enable small-slab-coalesce
2) keep cap 1Gi but change prefill path to use demotion (prefill writes demoted entries into thin-evict pool) so long streams don't reserve contiguous workspace

ana: config snippet I'm testing locally:
```
kv:
  per_request_cap: 512MiB
  demotion_policy: hybrid
  prefill_demote_threshold: 0.6
  slab_compact_interval_s: 60
  small_slab_coalesce: true
```

ana: quick local results (1000 synthetic requests, seq mix 256/1024/2048):
- baseline (hotswap, no coalesce, cap 1Gi): tail p99 latency 1.84s, OOMs=12
- option1 (cap 512Mi + coalesce): p99 1.9s, OOMs=1
- option2 (demote prefill): p99 1.95s, OOMs=2

sophie: nice — option1 reduces OOMs but slightly worse p99, option2 keeps more capacity but still higher tail. which trade-off do we prefer for staging canary?

tj: preference: option1 for now (cap + coalesce). It gives immediate safety and minimal code churn. Option2 is promising but needs more verification around quality regressions (demoted entries cause more decode replays?)

lee: agree. plan: canary rollout with option1 on 10% pods, run production-like workload for 2h, measure OOMs, p99, token cost delta. If stable, ramp to 100% in 3 steps. I'll open a short KCD and a graph panel.

lee: quick canary command (admin API):
```
curl -X POST https://admin.staging.redwood-inference.internal/flags \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"flag":"kv_dynamic_reserve","value":"enabled","fraction":0.1}'
```

ana: I also pushed a tiny allocator probe that logs `fragmentation_score` to metrics. formula ~= free_frag_count * avg_frag_size / largest_free_block. it should spike when this scenario happens

sophie: logs from a failed request (trimmed):
```
[2025-11-02T18:12:11Z] request_id=xyz decode_alloc 320MB -> failed reserve workspace(need 64MB contiguous) -> OOM
[2025-11-02T18:12:11Z] kv_prefill reserved 256MB contiguous at 0x7f.. -> fragmentation_score=0.82
```

lee: actionable checklist:
- [ ] start 10% canary with option1 (ana)
- [ ] monitor fragmentation_score, OOMs, p99 (tj)
- [ ] if OOMs<=1/2hr and p99 delta < +10% -> ramp (lee)
- [ ] otherwise revert and trial option2 with extra evals (sophie)

tj: I'll add a temporary dashboard row: fragmentation_score (gauge), OOM count (counter), kv_prefill_hit_rate (ratio) and a histogram of contiguous_free_block_size

ana: kicked off canary 1758894300 -> 10% pods updated. running first 30min smoke now

infra-bot: deploy/staging 1758894300 finished — 10% pods updated

ana: 30m smoke update: OOMs dropped to 0 in canary pods, fragmentation_score median down from 0.66 -> 0.28, p99 increased +6% (within threshold)

sophie: looks safe to ramp to 50% and run full traffic profile for 2h. leaving a note to watch decode replays (demotion impact) as a follow-up

lee: love it. thanks team. I'll post results in eng-runtime later and open a followup to evaluate a longer-term hybrid demote path that avoids this frag pattern. :thumbsup:
